why: Two implementations of the same alignment ship in this repository: Python, for
`tooltrace shadow`, and TypeScript, for the dashboard's run diff. They cannot be
one implementation -- the dashboard aligns two runs a user picked, in the browser,
with no server -- so the risk is that they drift into disagreeing about what 'the
same decision' means. A reader comparing the same two runs in the CLI and in the
dashboard would then get two different answers about where they diverged.
Both test suites read this file. A case added here has to pass in both.
Each step is [tool, resource]. `sides` is the expected row kind per aligned row:

cases.name: identical runs align row for row
an extra step does not push the rest out of register
cases.why: The exact failure a positional zip has: every row after the extra step would compare unrelated calls.

cases.name: the same tool on a different resource is a different decision
a trailing step on the recorded side is reported
a leading step on the candidate side is reported
an empty candidate leaves every recorded step unmatched
two empty traces align to nothing
a reordering is two moves, not one match
cases.why: Order carries meaning: reading after writing is a different trajectory from reading before it.

cases.name: a longer shared run is preferred over an earlier single match
cases.why: A greedy first-match aligner takes the early pair and loses the run of three that follows.
